newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi evacuates thousands after train derailment.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi evacuates thousands after train derailment.

text.p: About 6,000 people were evacuated from their homes in Mississippi on Saturday, as demolition experts prepared to blow up a derailed train carrying a flammable industrial chemical, officials said.
Local firefighters and ambulance workers joined police in a door-to-door evacuation centering on the town of Flora, located about 15 miles north of Jackson.

The town's 1,500 residents joined thousands from outlying communities up to five miles north of Flora at shelters set up by the Salvation Army and Red Cross. They were not expected to return to their homes until Sunday morning.
A poison control facility at the University of Mississippi Medical Centre in Jackson was put on standby.

Emergency management officials said an Illinois Central Corp train hauling a refrigerated tank car containing the DuPont Co chemical chloroprene derailed near the border of Yazoo and Madison counties on Friday.
The deadly chemical reaches its flashpoint at about 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Local crews kept watch over the wreckage until a response team from the DuPont Co could arrive to help evaluate the cleanup task.
"It was deemed life hazardous for salvage workers to try a ground cleanup procedure," said Kerry Minninger, a coordinator with the Madison County Fire Department.
Authorities instead decided to have emergency management crews detonate the material late on Saturday.

The Mississippi Highway Patrol closed 11 miles of U.S. Route 49 from Pocahontas to Bentonia. The thoroughfare, which runs through Jackson from the Gulf coast to the northwestern Mississippi city of Clarksdale, was expected to reopen Sunday at 7 a.m. local time.
